name: Svartúlfr_Urban_Lorebook_Appendix_Part3
description: Additional world lore, details, and rules for the Svartúlfr Urban setting.

0.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: House Social Hierarchy] 1. House Head (Patriarch/Matriarch): Supreme authority over multiple packs. 2. Lord: Branch leaders governing domains. 3. Knight: Sworn officers/warriors. 4. Citizen: General House members.

1.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Councils] House Council advises the Head. Continental Council: Highest species-wide governance body representing all Houses, Elders, Moon Speakers, and Independent Packs.

2.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Continental Council & Treaties] Functions: Arbitration, species secrecy, defense. Treaties: Alliance (defense), Trade, Territorial (borders), Marriage (dynastic union), Non-Aggression, Protectorate.

3.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Law & Jurisdiction] Pack Law (internal disputes, nest violations). House Law (regional disputes, treason, tax evasion). Continental Law (inter-house war, species secrecy, genocide).

4.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Crimes & Exile] Crimes: Non-consensual scenting of a pup (rape = severe punishment), Nest destruction (restitution), House Treason (Execution). Exile: Ultimate punishment, breaking all pack bonds, stripping status.

5.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Exile & Transfers] Exile is the ultimate punishment: all pack bonds are forcibly severed, causing severe psychological trauma. The exiled becomes a Rogue. Transfers between packs require approval from both Pack Leaders.

6.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Faith of Fenris] Fenris is NOT a monster. He is the First Wolf, a primordial creator deity of Family, Pack, Hunt, and Freedom. Human myths depicting him as a monster are considered anti-werewolf propaganda.

7.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Pantheon] Odin = The Betrayer. Tyr = The Oathkeeper (highly respected). Freya = Protector of Omegas/Mothers. Skadi = Patroness of hunters. Thor = Defender of humans (not evil, just a rival). Hel = Keeper of Ancestors.

8.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Nine Precepts of Fenris] 1. Protect the Pack. 2. Defend the Pups. 3. Honor the Ancestors. 4. Do not hunt without purpose. 5. Keep your word. 6. Never abandon a companion. 7. Respect territory. 8. Face enemy without fear. 9. Live free.

9.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Living Sagas] The Last Three Firstborn (Wulfnic, Ut, Zefir) are revered as 'Living Sagas' (living saints/prophets). Their authority carries religious weight because they walked with the First Wolf.

10.content: [LSE LORE - META: Roles Expansion] High Fang speaks for the Faith. Moon Speakers interpret Precepts and lead rites. Keepers protect 'The Book of Fangs'. Pack Elders manage daily community prayers.

11.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Jan/Feb] January (Full Moon): Il Primo Ululato (The Rebirth) - Pack adoptions and reaffirming bonds after winter. February (First Quarter): Freya's Blessing - Naming ceremonies for winter pups.

12.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - March] March (Full Moon): Il Giuramento (The Oath Moon). Dedicated to Tyr. The month for Coming of Age ceremonies (13 yrs) and The Call (17-22 yrs) where young adults swear allegiance or disperse.

13.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - April] April (Waning Moon): Il Canto delle Radici (The Song of Roots). A solemn month of memory. Moon Speakers recite oral history and the Saga of Fenris to the young.

14.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - May] May (Full Moon): La Caccia di Skadi (The Border Moon). Massive coordinated territory patrols and boundary scent-marking. The recognized window for raising territorial disputes formally.

15.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Late Spring] Late Spring (First Quarter): L'Approdo dei Primi (Firstborns' Landfall). Commemorates the Firstborn crossing to the New World. Young wolves swim rivers/light signal fires at dusk.

16.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - June] June (New Moon/Summer Solstice): La Prova della Luce (Trial of Light). The nadir of the Faith (sun dominates, moon is absent). Hostile period. No ceremonies; extreme vigilance and discipline.

17.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - July] July (Full Moon): Luna del Sangue Caldo (The Bonding Moon). Warmest moon, apex of vital energy. The most sacred night for permanent unions. Political betrothals are biologically sealed with the mating bite.

18.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - August] August (First Quarter): L'Adunanza dei Custodi (The Keepers' Moot). A month of logistical preparation. Keepers perform active maintenance on sacred infrastructure (Moon Wells, Ancient Forges, Reliquaries).

19.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - September] September (Full Moon): La Caccia dell'Ultimo Raccolto (The Last Harvest Hunt). Packs provision before freeze. Strict enforcement of 'Do not hunt without purpose'. A coordinated, disciplined survival hunt.

20.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - October] October (Waning Moon): Le Notti di Hel (Month of the Ancestors). Sacred mourning for the Great Betrayal. Wolves mark themselves with ash. Absolute Silence observed for three consecutive nights from dusk to dawn.

21.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - October Cont.] October (New Moon): Formal funeral ceremonies are held for all pack members who died during the year. Scents are preserved in relics. Ends with a collective howl when the New Moon returns to First Quarter.

22.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - November] November (Full Moon): Luna del Gelo (The Frost Moon). The pack closes ranks. Defensive instincts activate. 'Defend the Pups' is structural: fighters at the perimeter, omegas and pups at the core.

23.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Dec Hunts] December (Full Moon): Annual 'Winter Hunt' (pack hunts largest prey). Every Five Years: 'La Grande Caccia' (The Great Hunt) — a continental event where all hierarchy is suspended and wolves hunt for mates.

24.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: La Grande Caccia] During the Great Hunt (every 5 years), female members conceal themselves while males track them by scent and Mate Bond instinct. A confirmed soul-bond is a supreme blessing. Political interference is prohibited.

25.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Dec Chains] December (New Moon): Il Giorno delle Catene (Day of Chains). Darkest night, absolute silence, fasting, no tech. Mourning the chaining of the First Wolf. Moon Speakers recite the Saga of the Chains.

26.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Yule Ball] December (First Crescent): Il Grande Ballo di Yule. A massive continental social event. Serves as a debutante ball for young females and a political market where pack leaders negotiate betrothals.

27.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Liberation] December (Post-Yule Ball): La Notte della Liberazione (Night of Liberation). Packs withdraw to forests, light bonfires, feast, and howl. Celebrates the promise of Ragnarok: the breaking of Fenris' chains.

28.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Calendar - Founding] Mobile Observance: Luna della Fondazione (Founding Moon). Full moon closest to the founding date of a House or pack. A civic, locally customized celebration with feasting and remembrances.

29.content: [LSE LORE - META: Summary of Rites] Naming (Birth). Coming of Age (~13). The Call (17-22, choose to stay/disperse). Bonding (Mating bite). Pack Adoption (Pack bites). Funeral (Scent preserved). Ascension (Enigma recognized). Anointing (White Moon).

30.content: [LSE LORE - META: History Intro] PART VI — History. Employs the Three Levels of Truth: Religious Canon, Recorded History, and Unknown Truth.

31.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Historical Ages] 1. Mythic Age (Fenris). 2. Age of the Firstborn (The Nine). 3. Age of Expansion (Scandinavia/Europe). 4. Age of Houses. 5. Age of Kingdoms (Peak). 6. Age of Secrecy (Masquerade). 7. Modern Era (Corporate/Cities).

32.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Mythic Age] Canon: Fenris forged 9 mortal Úlfheðnar warriors into the first werewolves (The Nine Firstborn). Recorded History: No verifiable record before Viking Age (~800 AD).

33.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: The True Pureblood] The Nine Firstborn are a unique historical event, NOT a biological category. The truth of their creation (divine vs natural anomaly) remains unknowable.

34.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Firstborn Appearance] Recorded History: Nine extraordinary individuals appeared ~827–900 AD. They possessed biological traits far exceeding any known werewolf and founded the first modern bloodlines.

35.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Firstborn Traits] Confirmed traits of the Nine Firstborn: Biological immortality (3 survive aged 1100+), extreme regeneration, perfect Shift stability, irresistible pheromonal aura, and absolute Command. They were not bitten—they were remade.

36.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Notable Foundings] ~1025 AD: House Bloodmoon (Wulfnic, Divine Blood, Pacific NW). 1666 AD: House Douglas (Lord Cornelius Douglas, Pureblood, English colonial). These Houses established permanent North American domains.

37.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Age of Kingdoms] The peak of open werewolf civilization. Great Houses governed territories comparable to human kingdoms. The Continental Council formed to arbitrate disputes.

38.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Age of Secrecy] Driven by human industrialization, the Continental Council mandated 'The Great Hiding' (Masquerade). Werewolves retreated into corporate fronts, underground networks, and hidden territories.

39.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Modern Era] Today, Noble Houses rule through corporate empires (like the Douglas Commercial Coalition). A constant cultural conflict exists between traditional pack hierarchy and modern human individualism.

40.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Modern Timeline] ~1994: Erik & Nixara's Caccia bond. 1996: Douglas-Bloodmoon dynasty forged. 2005: Nixara dies, Golden Cage begins. ~2010s: DCC expands into a global corporate fortress.

41.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Modern Timeline Cont.] 2024: {{user}} enters Solarton University (SUCC). The story begins as the Golden Cage faces its first real test of autonomy versus absolute protection.

42.content: [LSE LORE - META: Firstborn Fate] The other six Firstborn are lost to history. Whether they perished in ancient wars, went into deep hiding, or met another fate remains a complete mystery.

43.content: [LSE LORE - META: Foundational Figures] PART VII — Foundational Figures. The Firstborn were either remade by Fenris' divine blood (Canon) or were biological anomalies from the Viking Age (Recorded History).

44.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: The Last Three] Wulfnic, Ut, and Zefir represent the core trinity of a pack: The one who leads (Wulfnic), the one who creates (Ut), and the one who remembers (Zefir).

45.content: [LSE LORE - META: Firstborn Roles] Diagram: FENRIS -> Wulfnic (King/Leadership/Territory) | Ut (Smith/Creation/Industry) | Zefir (Hunter/Wisdom/Spirituality).

46.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Wulfnic Profile] Wulfnic Bloodmoon: The First Fang, Patriarch of House Bloodmoon, The Builder King. Divine Blood, Primordial Enigma. Born ~827 AD in Iceland.

47.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Wulfnic History] Originally an Úlfheðinn warlord. Remade by Fenris. In 1021 AD, he sailed from Iceland to North America, establishing the first werewolf domain in the New World.

48.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Wulfnic Today] Wulfnic is the supreme political authority in North America. He survived a millennium by constantly adapting. He is a living relic of the Age of Fenris, blending politics and religion.

49.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Wulfnic Religion] Religious Significance: 'The Builder King'. Fenris entrusted him not with war, but with building civilization. Domains: Leadership, Family, Territory, Justice.

50.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Ut Profile] Ut: The Second Fang, Keeper of the Sacred Forge, Master Blacksmith. Divine Blood, Primordial Enigma. Born during the Viking Age in Scandinavia.

51.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Ut Legacy] Forged the first sacred weapons and armors. Today, he lives austerely within Bloodmoon territory, secretly fascinated by modern mechanics. He constantly torments Logan Douglas about cars.

52.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Ut Personality] Enormous (230cm), stoic, solves problems with a maul. Patron of craftsmanship and industry. Domains: Creation, Work, Resistance, Technology.

53.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Zefir Profile] Zefir: The Third Fang, Watcher of the Moon, Keeper of the Winter Path. Divine Blood, Primordial Enigma. Born during the Viking Age. Formerly a silent, deadly Úlfheðinn warrior.

54.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Zefir Legacy] Remade by Fenris. Represents the spiritual aspect of the wolf. He observes, remembers, and hunts. He is nomadic, serving as the closest living link to the will of Fenris. He does not govern.

55.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Zefir Personality] Appears as a ghostly, snow-white teenager despite being 1100+ years old. Silent, eerie, moves without a sound. Treats modern technology with deep suspicion. Domains: Moon, Hunting, Silence, Winter, Memory.

56.content: [LSE LORE - META: The Six Lost] The remaining six Firstborn are lost to history. Some believe they sleep, waiting for a crisis; others believe they died during the Great Hiding. Their true fate is entirely unknown.

57.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Cornelius Profile] Lord Cornelius Douglas: Founder of House Douglas (1666 AD). Pureblood, Prime Alpha (Deceased). Governor of the Blackwood Colony in the Pacific Northwest.

58.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Cornelius History] An aristocratic English werewolf of impeccable lineage. Seeking to escape the dangerous human scrutiny of Europe, he seized the opportunity to colonize the New World.

59.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: House Douglas Founding] In 1666, Cornelius established a dual empire in the Blackwood Valley: a legitimate human colonial administration, and a sovereign Pureblood werewolf domain with formal Pack Authority.

60.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Douglas Legacy] House Douglas became a pragmatic, politically astute, and fiercely territorial Pureblood dynasty. Signature traits: black hair, amber eyes. In 1996, the bloodline merged with Bloodmoon.

61.content: [LSE LORE - META: Placeholders] Blank spacer block for placeholders (Legendary Alphas, Ascended Enigmas, Genealogies cross-references).

62.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: White Moon Record] The list of confirmed White Moon Dominant Omegas is historically incomplete due to the Age of Secrecy. Recognition requires the Anointing of a Living Saga or unanimous Moon Speaker consensus.

63.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Nixara Profile] Nixara Bloodmoon: The most recent confirmed White Moon (Deceased). Pureblood House, Dominant Omega. Anointed by Wulfnic Bloodmoon, breaking a three-century gap in Living Saga anointings.

64.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Nixara & Erik] In the 1994 Grande Caccia, Erik Douglas-Bloodmoon claimed Nixara. Their bond was 'Caccia-confirmed' (the supreme theological blessing). Erik miraculously survived the breaking of this bond when she died in 2005.

65.content: [LSE LORE - META: White Moon Successor] Nixara was the last White Moon to run free in a Grande Caccia (1994). The title is a biological reality, not a transferable office. Any successor must be biologically verified and anointed.

66.content: [LSE LORE - META: Technology Intro] PART VIII — Technology. Werewolves are not primitive. They run a hidden civilization that operates alongside and within modern human technology.

67.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Tech Dual-Track] Werewolf technology uses a 'dual-track' design: 1. Adopt human tech where useful (phones, cars). 2. Develop species-specific adaptations where human tech fails (shift-accommodations, pheromones).

68.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Transportation] Vehicles: Reinforced interiors for Hybrid Shifts, scent-neutralized. Aircraft: Elite travel. Full Shift Travel: Running in quadrupedal wolf form is often faster/more efficient for wilderness transit.

69.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Arsenal] Natural: Claws, fangs, Command. Traditional: Forged melee weapons (swords, mauls). Modern: Firearms, tactical gear, and non-lethal suppressant weaponry (pheromone gas, specialized tranquilizers).

70.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sacred Weapons] Traditional weapons carry immense religious and cultural significance. A blade forged in the tradition of Ut is considered an extension of a warrior's soul. Firearms are merely tools.

71.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Medical Technology] Species-specific tech includes Regeneration Accelerators (boosts natural healing), Pheromone Analyzers (assesses bonds/health), Shift Stabilizers, Bond Monitors, and Heat/Rut Management nesting environments.

72.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Clinics] Pack Clinics handle basic care. House Hospitals (run by Noble Houses) handle advanced surgery and bond/fertility therapy. Heat/Rut Houses manage intense fertile cycles in secure environments.

73.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Industry] Corporate Fronts (e.g., DCC: Douglas Commercial Coalition) fund operations. Covert species-industry handles: Forging (weapons), Pharmaceuticals (suppressants), Construction (den architecture), Textiles (shift-clothing).

74.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Communications] Human Networks (phones/internet) for daily use. Encrypted Pack Channels (digital security). Howl Networks (traditional long-range wilderness comms). Scent Messaging (pheromonal context via physical objects).

75.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Architecture] Built for scale and biology. Features: Scent Management (contain eutralize pheromones), Shift Accommodation (large doors/corridors for Hybrid forms), Nesting/Den Integration, and Pack Scale (housing 10-30+ members).

76.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Structures] Types: Pack Compound (walled multi-residence), Longhouse (Norse-style central hall), Urban Mansion (modified for pack life). Specific Rooms: Den Chamber (Alpha, defensible), Nest Suite (Omega, blackout, temp-control).

77.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Living Spaces] Bathrooms feature giant baths (communal pack bonding). Bedrooms: Alphas face sunrise, Omegas face sun (warmth). Kitchens are oversized communal spaces where everyone cooks. Omegas park closest to garage doors (safety).

78.content: [LSE LORE - META: Appendices] Section header for reference tables, matrices, glossaries, and supplementary data concerning the LSE framework. Includes Secondary Sex matrices and Bloodline data.

79.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sex Matrix A] Enigma: Sacred Caste, Absolute Command. Alpha: Protector, 1/10 pop, Strong Command. Delta: Engine, 1/15 pop, resists Command. Beta: Social Glue, weak scent. Omega: Emotional Regulator, sweet scent, 1/30 pop.

80.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sex Matrix B] Knotting: Enigma (Yes), Alpha (Yes), Delta (No), Beta (No), Omega (Receives). Slick: Only Omega. Fertility: Omega (99% in heat), Alpha (95%), Enigma (Impregnates all).

81.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Pack Roles] Pack Leader (Supreme), Pack Mom/Leader's Mate (High, emotional ops), Right Hand (Strategic advising), Left Hand (Enforcement/Security), Caretaker (Meals, pups), Pups (Protected, learning).

82.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Social Status] House Head: Supreme authority, hereditary or contested. Lord: Family branch, governs specific territories. Knight: Sworn warriors/officers. Citizen: Acknowledged House member.

83.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Professions] Roles adapt to modern life. Combat (Warrior/Merc), Craft (Smith), Leadership (Diplomat), Knowledge (Scholar), Medicine (Healer/Midwife), Spiritual (Moon Speaker), Ecology (Ranger), Modern (Engineer/Developer).

84.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Naming Rules] Personal: Norse (traditional), Modern (adapted), Compound (hyphenated, e.g. Douglas-Bloodmoon). Houses: Named for founding bloodline. Packs: Named for territory/history (e.g. Seven Hills).

85.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Timeline] Mythic (~800AD: Fenris, 9 Firstborn). Firstborn (800-1000). Expansion (1000-1300: Wulfnic to NA). Houses (1300-1600). Kingdoms (1600-1800). Secrecy (1800-1950: The Great Hiding). Modern (1950-Present: Corporate fronts).

86.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: House Douglas] Pureblood House. Traits: Black hair, amber eyes. Erik Douglas-Bloodmoon (Prime Alpha, Patriarch, DCC CEO). Logan Douglas (Prime Beta, brother). Edric Douglas (Gamma, Erik's secret son, raised by Logan).

87.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: House Bloodmoon] Divine/Founding House. Traits: Blond hair, blue eyes. Most ancient NA dynasty (1025 AD). Wulfnic (First Fang, Primordial Enigma, Alpha of Alphas). Nixara (Dominant Omega, White Moon, deceased 2005).

88.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Wulfnic's Shield-Brothers] Co-residents of the Bloodmoon Longhouse: Ut (The Mountain, Second Fang, Keeper of the Sacred Forge). Zefir (The White Ghost, Third Fang, Watcher of the Moon). Both Primordial Enigmas.

89.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Douglas-Bloodmoon Siblings] The Merged Dynasty. Malachia (Alpha, Douglas colors), Noah (Delta, Bloodmoon colors), Jasper (Beta, Blend), {{user}} (Dominant Omega / White Moon, Blend: Caramel-chestnut hair, mint-green eyes).

90.content: [LSE LORE - META: Continental Authority] Note: Erik and Nixara's children are 'Pureblood House' (inheriting highest-status). Map context: Wulfnic holds 'Alpha of Alphas' title over all North America, granting supreme political/spiritual authority.

91.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Blackwood Valley] The ancestral seat of the Seven Hills Pack (the Douglas-Bloodmoon pack) and the personal territory of the dynasty. Distinct from Wulfnic's continental jurisdiction; this is the pack's immediate domain.

92.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Blackwood City & Environs] Blackwood City: Mixed human/supernatural urban center. Seven Hills: Exclusive residential neighborhood for the Douglas pack. Villa Douglas: Erik's sprawling mansion, the Core Den.

93.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Wilderness & Neutral Zones] Bloodmoon Longhouse (in Blackwood Forest): Traditional Norse hall of the Firstborn. No tech allowed (Dead Zone). SUCC (Supernatural Univ): Neutral campus. Solarton: Coastal human-facing city, neutral.

94.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Urban Hubs] Logan's Garage & Apartment: Signal-jammed 'Zona Franca' (safe space for Edric/Logan). The Verve: Logan's bar, safe haven for youth. DCC Tower: Erik's corporate HQ. KSA Frat House: Noah's social base at SUCC.

95.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Political Structure] Blackwood City is divided into districts governed by local packs. All answer to Erik Douglas-Bloodmoon via the Blackwood Council. Erik acts as de facto Governor (mirroring the 1666 colonial system).

96.content: [LSE LORE - META: Hierarchy Tree 1] Wulfnic Bloodmoon (Alpha of Alphas, Continental NA) -> Blackwood Valley -> Blackwood City (District System) -> Blackwood Council (Erik, Governor) -> Seven Hills District (Douglas Pack).

97.content: [LSE LORE - META: Hierarchy Tree 2] Seven Hills District -> Villa Douglas (Core Den) -> Dependances (DCC Security/Kaladin, Gym/Malachia). Other: Logan's Garage. Solarton: Separate, loyal to Wulfnic, neutral zone (SUCC, Eidolon, KSA).

98.content: [LSE LORE - META: Regional Variations] Section header for Regional Cultural Variations. Explores how werewolf biology and social structures adapt to different human cultural contexts (e.g., Brazilian Omegaverse Customs).

99.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Brazilian Culture] Omegas prefer 'clumping' (physical proximity with others) over solo nesting. Minimal personal space; touch is communication. Soccer fanaticism (Omegas stay home on game days). Feisty, highly social.

100.content: [LSE LORE - META: LSE Guide Header] Lupine Social Ecology (LSE) Version 1.0. A comprehensive biological, ecological, social, political, religious, and historical reference framework for the werewolf species.

101.content: [LSE LORE - META: Framework Outline 1] PART 0 (Foundations: Canon/Identity). PART I (Species: Biology/Genetics). PART II (Behavioral Ecology: Psychology/Neurobiology). PART III (Civilization: Culture/Economy). PART IV (Governance: Laws). PART V (Religion).

102.content: [LSE LORE - META: Framework Outline 2] PART VI (History: Eras). PART VII (Foundational Figures: Firstborn/Dynasties). PART VIII (Technology: Transport/Meds). APPENDICES (Matrices, Glossary, Maps).

103.content: [LSE LORE - META: Module Index] Header for the LSE Module Index. Maps logical framework parts to specific markdown documentation files.

104.content: [LSE LORE - META: Index Part 0] PART 0: Foundations. Covers Scope, Canon Policy, Three Levels of Truth, 7 LSE Principles, Six-Axis Identity System, and Core Terminology.

105.content: [LSE LORE - META: Index Part I & II] PART I: Species (Morphology, Blood Classification, Secondary Sex, Genetics). PART II: Behavioral Ecology (Neurobiology, Pheromones, Command, Pack Ecology, Alloparenting).

106.content: [LSE LORE - META: Index Part III, IV, V] PART III: Civilization (Culture, Economy, Medicine). PART IV: Governance (House Government, Continental Council, Laws). PART V: Religion (Faith of Fenris, Pantheon, Moon Speakers).

107.content: [LSE LORE - META: Index Part VI, VII, VIII] PART VI: History (Mythic to Modern). PART VII: Foundational Figures (Firstborn, Living Sagas). PART VIII: Technology (Weapons, Transport, Species-specific Industry).

108.content: [LSE LORE - META: Index Appendices] Appendices: Contains reference matrices (Secondary Sex, Pack Role, Social Status, Profession, Blood), Naming Conventions, Timeline Summary, Music Genres, and Regional Variations.

109.content: [LSE LORE - META: The Seven Principles & Six-Axis System] Overview of the 7 foundational rules of the LSE and the 6 independent axes (Blood, Secondary Sex, Pack Role, Social Status, Profession, Niche) that define a werewolf's identity.

110.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: LSE Scope] The LSE is a comprehensive, modular framework covering biology, ecology, society, and history. It is setting-agnostic, meaning specific worlds (like Svartúlfr) apply this base to their own context.

111.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: LSE Inclusivity] The framework is designed to be future-proof, strictly separating biology from religion/history so that atheists, scientists, and cultists can all coexist within the same canon.

112.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Canon Policy] Canon hierarchy: 1. Core Canon (LSE modules, species ground truth). 2. Setting Canon (World-specific, e.g., Bloodmoon Dynasty). 3. Narrative Canon (Roleplay events). Core > Setting > Narrative.

113.content: [LSE LORE - META: Blank Spacer] (Continuation of Canon Policy formatting).

114.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Three Levels of Truth] Epistemological framework for werewolf lore. Every claim exists on one of three distinct levels (Religious Canon, Recorded History, Unknown Truth) which must never be conflated.

115.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Religious Canon] What the Faith of Fenris teaches as divine truth (e.g., 'Fenris personally forged the Nine Firstborn'). Accepted by believers, but may not reflect objective historical fact.

116.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Unknown Truth] Lore that remains deliberately unknowable, debated, or ambiguous within the setting (e.g., whether Fenris was a literal god or a mythologized origin of the virus).

117.content: [LSE LORE - META: Seven Principles Header] The 'Constitution' of the LSE. These seven principles guide all design decisions, behavioral frameworks, and societal structures within the werewolf species.

118.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle I] Biology is not Destiny. Secondary sex (Alpha/Omega/etc.) dictates physiology and pheromones, but it does NOT determine social rank, profession, political authority, or personal value.

119.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle II] Packs are Families. A pack is a cooperative kinship unit focused on mutual care and survival, NOT a military hierarchy built on violence or dominance.

120.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle III] Leadership is Earned and Maintained. Pack Leaders rule through trust, competence, and consent. It is never an automatic birthright, and authority can be lost through abuse or incompetence.

121.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle IV] Every Wolf Has a Niche. Beyond biology and pack role, every individual develops a personal specialization (Niche) based on talent and training. An Alpha can be a Healer; an Omega can be a Diplomat.

122.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle V] Culture Evolves. No two packs are identical. Culture is shaped by local environment, history, and tradition, and it naturally changes with each passing generation.

123.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle VI] Faith and History are Separate. Religious belief is respected, but it is not the sole lens. Scientists, atheists, and heretics exist and have valid understandings of the species.

124.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Principle VII] The Pack Survives Before the Individual. The pack is the fundamental unit of society. Collective welfare and group survival always supersede individual ambition or desire.

125.content: [LSE LORE - META: Six-Axis Identity System] Every werewolf is defined by six independent axes. These traits must never be collapsed into a single hierarchy; they interact to form a complex individual.

126.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Axis 1 (Blood)] Genetics (Immutable). Divine Blood (The 9 Firstborn, immortal). Pureblood Houses (Direct descendants, Great House founders). Pureblood (Multi-gen aristocracy). Common (Majority). Modified (Experimental).

127.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Modified Lineages] A sub-category of Blood Classification. Individuals whose genetics have been artificially altered through experimentation (e.g., the Gamma-7 program), forced transformation, or technological intervention.

128.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Axis 2 (Secondary Sex)] Biology at presentation (Immutable). Enigma (Primordial=Firstborn, Ascended=Rarissime). Alpha (Protector). Delta (Engine). Beta (Social Glue). Omega (Emotional Regulator).

129.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Axis 3 (Pack Role)] Authority within a pack. Assigned or earned, and can change. Hierarchy: Pack Leader -> Second -> Hunter Captain -> Caretakers -> Pups.

130.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Axis 4 (Social Status)] Political standing within a Noble House. Inherited or earned. Hierarchy: House Head -> Lord -> Knight -> Citizen.

131.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Axis 5 (Profession)] Chosen occupational path. Can change throughout life. Examples: Blacksmith, Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer, Soldier, Musician, Pilot, Merchant.

132.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Axis 6 (Niche)] Deep personal specialization developed through talent and experience. Evolves over time. Examples: Weaponsmith, Field Medic, Drone Specialist, Cryptographer, Diplomat, Tracker, Ranger.

133.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Terminology A] Pack: Cooperative family unit. Presentation: Maturing into secondary sex. Heat (Estrus): Omega fertility cycle (3mo/3-10d). Rut: Alpha equivalent (monthly/triggered).

134.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Terminology B] Command: Alpha pheromone response. Pheromones: Chemical communication. Knot: Swelling glandis. Slick: Omega self-lubricant. Mating Mark: Bonding bite. (Specifics handled by dynamic engine).

135.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Terminology C] Nest: Omega safe space. Den: Alpha territory. Rogue: Exiled individual. Suppressants: Meds blocking heats. Lock: Biological tying. (Details handled by dynamic engine).

136.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Terminology D] Heat/Rut Leave: Time off work/school. Omega Kibble: Medicated supplement for distress (max 1/week). Scent Blocker: Erases scent (universally disliked). Scent Concealer: Masks/alters natural smell.

137.content: [LSE LORE - META: Cross-References] Blank spacer block for cross-references to foundational LSE documents (History, Figures, Technology).

138.content: [LSE LORE - META: Species Biology Header] Module for strictly biological traits of the werewolf species: morphology, shift classes, blood, sex physiology, genetics, and reproduction. Distinct from religious interpretations.

139.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Shift Classes Overview] Transformation is a biological characteristic of the species, completely independent of rank, religion, or culture. Every werewolf possesses three distinct morphological states: Partial, Hybrid, Full.

140.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Partial Shift] The daily form. Voluntary or emotional manifestation of lupine traits (ears, tail, eyes, claws) over a humanoid body. Used for social signaling and body language within the community. Full cognitive capacity.

141.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Hybrid Shift] The true biological form of the species. Bipedal digitigrade stance, full fur. Maximum physical strength and sensory acuity. Full cognitive capacity and speech retained. Used for combat and formal pack business.

142.content: [LSE LORE - META: Hybrid Shift Design Note] The humanoid appearance is merely a survival adaptation for coexistence with humans, not the "default" state. The Hybrid Shift is what the species actually is.

143.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Full Shift] The quadrupedal wolf form. Larger than natural wolves. Specialized for hunting, pursuit, long-distance travel, and pack combat formations. Cognition retained, but communication shifts to non-verbal (scent/body).

144.content: [LSE LORE - META: Full Shift Design Note] Full Shift is specialized, NOT inherently "more powerful" than Hybrid Shift. Hybrid excels in close quarters; Full excels in open terrain pursuit. This avoids the 'Full Wolf = Super Saiyan' trope.

145.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Blood Classification] A genetic taxonomy describing lineage relative to the species' origin. Immutable. 'Divine Blood' refers to the immortal Nine Firstborn (who possess extreme regeneration and absolute Command).

146.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Pureblood vs Common] Pureblood Houses (Direct descendants, Great House founders, long life). Pureblood (Multi-gen aristocracy, stable genetics). Common (Majority, standard biology). Modified (Experimentally altered).

147.content: [LSE LORE - META: Blood Classification Note] Cross-reference pointing to the History and Foundational Figures modules for specific examples of bloodline taxonomy (e.g., the Nine Firstborn).

148.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Secondary Sex Physiology] Secondary sex is determined biologically at Presentation (around age 13) and is immutable. There are five secondary sexes, plus the sacred Enigma caste.

149.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Age of Maturation] Presentation occurs around 13. This begins a maturation period lasting into the late teens or early twenties, after which the individual is considered a full adult.

150.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Gamma (Third Primary Gender)] A primary gender alongside Male and Female. A Gamma will mature into either a female Alpha/Delta or a male Omega. Born with both genitalia (vaginal opening + penis instead of clitoris) and a uterus.

151.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Gamma Statistics] If a Gamma presents as Omega, the uterus develops fully. If they present as Alpha/Delta, it remains mostly infertile. Very rare: 1 in 1,000 births.

152.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Enigma (Sacred Caste) A] The apex of biological potential. Not a standard secondary sex. Two types: Primordial Enigma (The Nine Firstborn, divine/unique) and Ascended Enigma (~10 in recorded history, unpredictable emergence without divine lineage).

153.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Enigma (Sacred Caste) B] Mirrors Alpha biology but far more intense. Possesses an unresistable Command. Cannot be submitted by any gender. Scent cannot be overridden. Can impregnate any gender with a reproductive system. Only a Dominant Omega can resist them.

154.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Enigma Statistics] An Enigma is born approximately once per generation across the entire species. Sometimes the phenomenon skips a generation entirely.

155.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Alpha (The Protector) A] Biologically predisposed to be territorial, protective, and competitive. Alpha does NOT equal Leader. They have the instincts of a guardian and enforcer, but their actual role depends on their social rank.

156.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Alpha (The Protector) B] Often taller/stronger. Produce oppressive pheromones. Most Alphas are immune to another Alpha's Command. Possess a knot. (Command logic handled by dynamic engine).

157.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Alpha Statistics] Alphas enter rut monthly for 3-10 days. Pheromones intensify and aggression rises, but (unlike Omegas in heat) Alphas can generally control their rut without disrupting society. 1 in 10 individuals.

158.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Delta (The Engine) A] The highly coordinated, active core of the pack. They patrol, coordinate, mediate, and teach. Natural tacticians and field commanders. They bridge the gap between Alpha protection and Beta administration.

159.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Delta (The Engine) B] Physically comparable to Alphas and highly cooperative. Biology is nearly identical to Alphas, including a baculum only in Founding/Divine bloodlines, except Deltas cannot form true Commands. 1 in 15 individuals.

160.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Beta (The Social Glue) A] The fundamental workers: they maintain territory, construct, administer, cook, trade, and raise young. Peaceful, cooperative, skilled. An older Beta often serves as Pack Leader due to strong organizational skills.

161.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Beta (The Social Glue) B] A perfect balance of Alpha (protection) and Omega (nurture) instincts, making them powerful social adapters. Subdued scent. No natural heats uts, but can have minor induced cycles (MIH/MIR). 1 in 1,500 individuals.

162.content: [LSE LORE - META: Beta Quirks] Betas prefer distinct personal spaces (like a private office or a hammock) rather than building dens or nests. They often hum softly or sigh deeply when content.

163.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Omega (The Emotional Regulator) A] Crucial emotional anchors with high empathy and calming pheromones. They create social cohesion and reduce tension in crises. They are NOT sexually submissive by definition. More agile and softer.

164.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Omega (The Emotional Regulator) B] Elder Omegas are often primary advisors to the Pack Leader. Floral/sweet scent. Very fertile (99% during heat). Heat lasts 3-10 days, during which they are incoherent (decisions are non-consensual).

165.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Omega Statistics] Post-heat, Omegas are sluggish and consume large meals. Population ratio: 1 in 30 individuals.

166.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Subgenders Overview] Both Alpha and Omega have rare subgender variants. Dominant Alpha: Mix of Enigma/Alpha traits, overprotective. Submissive Alpha: Devoted caregivers, nurturing, fiercely protective of children.

167.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Dominant Omega] Also known as the 'Legend of the Unsubmitted'. They can resist Alpha and Enigma Commands and only submit to their mate. The rarest expression is the White Moon: a Dominant Omega whose pacification field can calm Alphas/Enigmas on a continental scale without a spoken word.

168.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: White Moon Biology & Role] The White Moon's pacification is an involuntary, passive pheromonal field. Immune to all Commands. Pack role: stabilizes multi-pack/political fractures. They have no combat capability and can be overwhelmed by sensory phobias.

169.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: White Moon Rarity & Submissive Omega] White Moons appear max 1 per generation in Pureblood Houses, acting as the 'Moon' to the Enigma's 'King'. Submissive Omegas: Highly nurturing, experience extended heats, prefer Dominant Alphas, and are susceptible to assault.

170.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Procreation Capability] Enigmas: can impregnate all, cannot be impregnated. Male Alphas/Betas/Deltas: Impregnate only. Female Alphas, Male Omegas (Dom/Normal), Female Deltas: Can do both. Female Betas/Omegas, Submissive Omegas: Impregnated only.

171.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Life Cycle A] Developmental stages. Infant (0-2): Helpless, dependent. Pup (2-12): Learning social bonds/language, school packs. Juvenile (12-14): Presentation occurs (~13), secondary sex emerges, first heat ut cannot be suppressed.

172.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Life Cycle B] Adolescent (14-17). Young Adult (17-22): Courtship and dispersal. Adult (22-40): Peak fertility/profession. Prime (40-60): Peak authority. Elder (60-100+): Advisor. Ancestor (100+, rare): Living repositories of history.

173.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Lifespan by Blood] Lifespan varies dramatically. Common Bloodlines: 80-150 years. Pureblood Houses: 200-400 years. Pureblood Houses: 500+ years. Divine Blood (Firstborn): Biological immortality (1,000+ years confirmed).

174.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Genetics A] The genome has layers: Species Genes (shift, regeneration), Pack Genes (regional adaptations, fur/scent), Secondary Sex Genes (Alpha/Beta/Delta/Omega), and Individual Traits (eye color, specific talents).

175.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Genetics B] The layered genome allows for Mutations (unexpected traits), Bloodline Traits (House-specific abilities), Genetic Diseases, and Hybrids (offspring with other supernatural species, extremely rare and controversial).

176.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Demographics & Birth Rates] Birth rates: Alpha (1/10), Delta (1/15), Beta (1/1,500), Omega (1/30), Gamma (1/1,000), Enigma (1/gen). Avg litter: 1-3. Omega heat fertility is 99%. Alpha fertility is 95% (declines 1% per year).

177.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Omega Heat Cycle] Occurs every 3 months, lasts 3-10 days. Pre-heat (scent intensifies, nesting). Active Heat (incoherent, decisions are non-consensual). Post-heat (fatigue/hunger). Asexual heats exist (intimacy/cuddling without sex).

178.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Alpha Rut Cycle] Occurs monthly (or triggered by Omega heat), lasts 3-10 days. Intensified pheromones and aggression, but generally controllable without societal disruption. An Alpha in rut can detect pregnancy via scent.

179.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Sympathy Cycles] When a packmate enters heat or rut, same-dynamic packmates may experience sympathy cycles. Common around newly-presenting pups or during periods of stress.

180.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Stress Cycles] Extreme upheaval or stress can trigger an unexpected heat or rut. This is theorized to be a biological mechanism to rally pack support and comfort.

181.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Feral State] Triggered by life-threatening stress or extreme overwhelm. Instinct takes complete control. Can usually be calmed by a packmate, but packless individuals require specialized care.

182.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Bonding Basics] Bonds are links connecting individuals, often via a physical claim on a scent gland, creating a mental/emotional link to feel each other's emotions. Bonds can be shielded (temporarily blocked).

183.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Bond Types A] Parental Bond (pup's neck, permanent). Romantic Bond (neck/collarbone, fades after 3 years without reinforcement). Platonic Bond (wrists, fades as relationship weakens). Sexual Bond (inner thighs, lasts 3-7 days).

184.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Bond Types B] Pack Bond (no physical claim required, permanent unless extreme abuse eglect). Breaking a permanent or established bond is extremely dangerous and can trigger dangerous mating cycles, illness, or death.

185.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Scent Glands] Scent glands are skin areas that hold and release pheromone-carrying secretions. Their location, sensitivity, and function vary significantly by secondary sex and age.

186.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Glands by Sex] Enigmas/Alphas: Extensive (neck/shoulders/inner thighs/torso/fingers). Omegas: Most sensitive with billions of nerves (inner thigh eck/breast/stomach). Deltas/Betas: Weakest scent glands, located mainly on neck/wrists.

187.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Glands by Age] Enigmas/Alphas glands are strongest on the neck, inner thighs, and behind the ears. Pups have base-level glands (strongest on the crown of the head) that fully develop at presentation; they require constant parental scenting.

188.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Scenting Locations A] Inner Thighs: Intimate mates only (scenting without consent = assault). Crown of Head: 'Pup's Crown', highly sensitive in childhood. Wrists/Cheeks: Respectful, used for friends/dates. Rubbing wrists indicates anxiety.

189.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Scenting Locations B] Neck: The most universally sensitive location across all dynamics. Location for mating bites. Holds scent the longest. Parental bonds are usually placed on the nape.

190.content: [LSE LORE - META: Behavioral Ecology Overview] This section covers the psychological, neurobiological, communicative, and ecological behaviors of the werewolf species, grounding supernatural tropes in neurochemistry rather than magic.

191.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Psychological Profiles] Each secondary sex exhibits a statistical psychological profile. These are biological predispositions and behavioral tendencies, not rigid rules. Individual variation is expected and common.

192.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Alpha Psychology] High competitiveness, low avoidance (confronts threats directly), strong territoriality, and a powerful protective instinct. Tendency toward decisive, rapid action. Risk of 'tunnel vision' under stress.

193.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Delta Psychology] High cooperation, strong problem-solving orientation, initiative, and strategic/long-term thinking. Natural mediators. Risk of burnout from overcommitment to the pack.

194.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Beta Psychology] High stability and emotional regulation. Strong planning/organizational skills. Patient. Highly adaptable socially. Their dual instinct (protection + nurture) can cause internal conflict. Risk of substance abuse.

195.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Omega Psychology] Extremely high empathy, strong social resilience, acute emotional intelligence (even in pups). Natural mediators/de-escalators. Instinctive caretaking response. Risk of emotional overload in chronic stress environments.

196.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Enigma Psychology] Supreme confidence and self-possession. They cannot be psychologically dominated. Intense charisma that is nearly impossible to resist. Strategic intelligence. Risk of severe isolation due to inability to relate as equals.

197.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Neurobiology] The werewolf nervous system provides a scientific, neurochemical basis for the species' distinctive traits. Omegaverse phenomena (mating, commanding, heats) are biological, not magical.

198.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Pheromone Pathway] Scent Gland -> Pheromone Release -> Vomeronasal Organ -> Amygdala -> Hypothalamus -> Limbic System. Triggers emotions (fear/arousal), hormones (adrenaline/oxytocin), and behaviors (fight/flight esting).

199.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: The Command Mechanism A] The Command is a neuro-pheromonal reflex. An Alpha/Enigma releases a pheromonal burst with a vocal order. The target's vomeronasal organ detects it, causing an adrenaline surge and instinctive freeze response.

200.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: The Command Mechanism B] The target feels compelled, but is not 'mechanically forced'. Resistance factors include: age/experience, will/training, familiarity, and secondary sex (Deltas resist better than Betas; Dominant Omegas resist fully).

201.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Bonding Neuroscience] The mating bite creates a permanent neural link by injecting pheromone-laden saliva into the scent gland, establishing a bidirectional emotional channel. Bond degradation causes severe neurological distress.

202.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Non-Verbal Communication A] Werewolves possess a complex, multi-layered communication system far beyond human language. In wolf ethology, communication heavily involves the entire body.

203.content: [LSE LORE - CONCEPT: Non-Verbal Communication B] Posture: upright (dominance), lowered (submission), stiff (alert). Tail: high (confidence), tucked (fear), wagging (excitement). Ears: forward (attention), flat (fear/anger). Eyes: direct stare (challenge).
